name: Priya Shah

five_sec.what_is_it: A recipe organizer with a meal planning calendar and an automatic grocery list.
five_sec.who_for: Home cooks who already have their own recipes.
five_sec.trust_why: Both store ratings shown, and 'no card required' is stated without qualification.
five_sec.next_step: Look for allergy or dietary settings.
five_sec.delivers_food_why: 'Recipes, Meal Plans and Grocery Lists, All in One App.' Software, not food.

full_page.what_stopped_me: Nothing about allergens or per-person settings. It's my recipes, so the filtering is still my job every Sunday. No way for the kids to weigh in.
full_page.whats_missing: Allergy handling, a way for the family to choose, named grocery stores.

PTE.quote: Clean, honest pricing and a 60-day refund. But nothing on this page about allergens or letting my kids weigh in; it's my recipes, my problem.

five_sec.what_is_it: A weekly dinner planner where the whole household votes by text, then the list goes to Instacart or Walmart.
five_sec.who_for: Families where everyone has opinions about dinner. Mine.
five_sec.trust_why: 'Your family votes on dinner by text' is precisely my problem. Small company, though, and I need to see how allergies are handled before I trust it.
five_sec.next_step: Scroll for per-person settings and allergy language.
five_sec.delivers_food_why: 'We don't deliver food. We plan your week and send your grocery list.'

full_page.what_stopped_me: No vegetarian sample week; the examples are chicken tenders and meatballs. 'Nut allergies ... are respected on every plan' is a strong claim with no detail on peanut versus tree nut or how ingredients are checked. And my 6-year-old has no phone, so how does he vote?
full_page.whats_missing: How the allergy filter works, a vegetarian sample week, how a child without a phone votes, Fry's named under the Kroger cart.

DD.quote: A profile per person with allergies, plus 'Always check ingredient labels' is the right level of caution. My 6-year-old has no phone, though.

five_sec.what_is_it: Meal kit delivery with a prize pop-up.
five_sec.who_for: People who don't mind a weekly box and a weekly bill.
five_sec.trust_why: 'Open A Box To Reveal Your Offer.' After Home Chef, gamified offers make me more careful, not less.
five_sec.next_step: Continue Without Offer, check the veggie plan.

full_page.what_stopped_me: Auto-renewing, price only after a zip, and I counted several recipes with peanuts in a shared-ingredient box. No per-person allergy settings.

HF.quote: Peanuts in the Thai grain salad and the ginger bowls, and a mystery-box pop-up. Home Chef already taught me this lesson.

five_sec.what_is_it: Weekly meal plans with a shopping list.
five_sec.who_for: Families wanting new recipes each week.
five_sec.trust_why: Professional, but no information above the fold.
five_sec.delivers_food_why: A phone with a checklist and 'Choose Your Meals'.

full_page.what_stopped_me: One plan for the whole family, no per-person allergy settings, no kids' input. The price and the cancel steps aren't on the page.

EM.quote: A Plant Based plan and 'registered dietitians' are reassuring. No per-person allergy settings, and I'd want the cancel steps before any trial.

five_sec.trust_why: The page is titled 'AI Meal Planning' and the main button is a CEO letter, not information.

full_page.what_stopped_me: Recipes are written by Ollie's AI for you. With a peanut allergy in the house that's a hard no. Then $25 a month on the pricing page.
full_page.whats_missing: Tested recipes, allergy policy, a price that matches across pages.

OL.quote: An AI that writes 'a recipe just for you' around my son's peanut allergy is contraindicated. Also, $25 a month.

dd_offer.why: No card, Family features free for 14 days, and the FAQ states that without a card you go back to the free plan. Cancel in one tap is stated too.
dd_offer.expect_day_15: Family features (texting, profiles, Kroger cart) end and the account reverts to Free. Nothing is billed without a card.

head_to_head.reason: It's the only one with per-person allergy and won't-eat profiles and a way for my kids to choose the menu, with a Kroger cart.

EM.reason: Per-person allergy profiles and family voting versus one plan for everyone.

PTE.reason: Plan to Eat is more polished, but DinnerDrop handles allergies and lets the kids vote.

OL.reason: No AI-written recipes near a peanut allergy.

HF.reason: No box with peanut recipes, no auto-renew.

dd_fix_that_would_move_me: Home page FAQ: add 'How do allergies work?' explaining what the per-person allergy setting removes (peanut vs tree nut, hidden ingredients) and its limits, and add a vegetarian tab to 'See a week'.
